answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. The protocol caps influence by locked stake, so splitting funds among a hundred umber, river, and violet identities does not multiply voting power; each identity merely divides the same stake. A sybil attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens to gain influence, paying acquisition costs and giving up liquidity while honest agents can still verify work and challenge claims.
